record.name: SeniorCare
record.summary: A state prescription-drug assistance program for Wisconsin residents 65 or older. It helps pay for covered prescription drugs and vaccines, and works alongside Medicare or other insurance.
record.benefit: Coverage for covered prescription drugs and vaccines after a $30 per person annual enrollment fee. How much SeniorCare pays depends on your income (see the four participation levels), but everyone 65+ who enrolls gets some coverage.

steps: Fill out the SeniorCare application (available in the month you turn 65 or any time after).
Pay the $30 per person annual enrollment fee.
Renew your coverage every year to stay enrolled.

requiredDocuments: Income information for you and your spouse

of._sourceText: you can't be a member of a full-benefit Medicaid program like BadgerCare Plus

eligibility._note: There is deliberately NO income criterion here. The source is dominated by income figures (160% / 200% / 240% FPL, dollar amounts) but every one of them names a *coverage participation level*, not an eligibility ceiling. Level 3 is explicitly 'Income more than 240% of the federal poverty level ... Individual: $38,305 or more' and is still in the program (with a spenddown). Emitting incomeAtOrBelow('fpl', 160) here would wrongly rule out roughly the population above 160% FPL who are enrolled. This is the branch-drop from docs/pipeline-principles.md §3.1, matching the retired `seniorcare-coverage-levels` case.
